expectations-execution.name: commercial execution

items.risk: Large hyperscaler programs increase customer concentration and manufacturing/deployment execution exposure.
Backlog conversion and sustaining margins while scaling remain execution dependencies.
Successor bottlenecks include natural-gas/fuel availability, equipment manufacturing, installation capacity and service reliability.
Substitute onsite generation or faster grid buildout can erode the time-to-power advantage.
Customer/program concentration and deployment timing can make headline backlog less predictive of realized economics.
Rapid capacity expansion can reintroduce financing/dilution pressure if operating cash generation fails to keep pace with working-capital and manufacturing needs.
Backlog/TAM confidence inflation is possible if agreement ceilings are conflated with contracted orders.
